title: Your Own Skin: The Slow Stroke

scenes.tts: A soft brush strokes your forearm. Does some nerve fibre care how fast it moves?
scenes.visual: A soft brush over a forearm. Title card: Your own skin, the slow stroke.
scenes.narration: A soft brush strokes your forearm. Does some nerve fibre care how fast it moves?

scenes.tts: Mouse genetics cannot be done in people. So human touch classes rest on another method, micro neur ography.
scenes.visual: A forearm and hand. Label: microneurography.
scenes.caption: Mouse genetics cannot be done in people. So human touch classes rest on another method, microneurography.
scenes.narration: Mouse genetics cannot be done in people. So human touch classes rest on another method, microneurography.

scenes.tts: A fine tungsten electrode goes through the skin into a nerve, in a conscious person. It records single afferents.
scenes.visual: A fine electrode enters a forearm nerve; a single unit spike train scrolls on a monitor.
scenes.narration: A fine tungsten electrode goes through the skin into a nerve, in a conscious person. It records single afferents.

scenes.tts: Recordings from the hand sorted human afferents into four classes, by firing. The ending is never seen.
scenes.visual: Four labels appear: RA, PC, SA I, SA II. Label: Johansson and Vallbo, 1979. An ending is drawn as a grey question mark.
scenes.narration: Recordings from the hand sorted human afferents into four classes, by firing. The ending is never seen.

scenes.tts: Hairy skin adds another class. Slow, unmyelinated afferents that respond to gentle deformation.
scenes.visual: Forearm hairy skin; a thin unmyelinated fibre lights up. Label: Vallbo and colleagues, 1999.
scenes.narration: Hairy skin adds another class. Slow, unmyelinated afferents that respond to gentle deformation.

scenes.tts: These are the C tactile afferents, physiologically similar to mouse C L T M Rs.
scenes.visual: Side by side: human CT afferent and mouse C-LTMR.
scenes.caption: These are the C-tactile afferents, physiologically similar to mouse C-LTMRs.
scenes.narration: These are the C-tactile afferents, physiologically similar to mouse C-LTMRs.

scenes.tts: The brush strokes from very slow to fast. Which speed drives a C tactile afferent hardest?
scenes.visual: Brush speeds marked along an axis from slow to fast. On screen: which speed?
scenes.caption: The brush strokes from very slow to fast. Which speed drives a C-tactile afferent hardest?
scenes.narration: The brush strokes from very slow to fast. Which speed drives a C-tactile afferent hardest?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: Not the fastest. C tactile firing rises, then falls, an inverted U. It peaks in the slow stroke range.
scenes.visual: CT firing draws as an inverted U across brushing velocity. On screen: peak about 1 to 10 cm/s (Löken and colleagues, 2009).
scenes.caption: Not the fastest. C-tactile firing rises, then falls: an inverted U. It peaks in the slow-stroke range.
scenes.narration: Not the fastest. C-tactile firing rises, then falls: an inverted U. It peaks in the slow-stroke range.

scenes.tts: Pleasantness ratings correlated with that firing. Fast myelinated A beta afferents behaved differently. Their firing kept rising with speed.
scenes.visual: Pleasantness ratings trace the same inverted U; a second curve, Aβ firing, climbs steadily with velocity.
scenes.caption: Pleasantness ratings correlated with that firing. Fast myelinated Aβ afferents behaved differently. Their firing kept rising with speed.
scenes.narration: Pleasantness ratings correlated with that firing. Fast myelinated Aβ afferents behaved differently. Their firing kept rising with speed.

scenes.tts: Reviews conclude that these afferents support gentle, affective touch, the social side of touch.
scenes.visual: Two hands, one stroking the other forearm. Label: affective touch.
scenes.narration: Reviews conclude that these afferents support gentle, affective touch, the social side of touch.

scenes.tts: But not every affective touch relies on them. And affective touch need not be pleasant.
scenes.visual: On screen: not every affective touch relies on CTs.
scenes.narration: But not every affective touch relies on them. And affective touch need not be pleasant.

scenes.tts: The human C tactile ending is still unknown. The mouse hair map cannot be transplanted onto human hair.
scenes.visual: The mouse follicle map slides toward a human hair and stops, marked with a question mark.
scenes.caption: The human C-tactile ending is still unknown. The mouse hair map cannot be transplanted onto human hair.
scenes.narration: The human C-tactile ending is still unknown. The mouse hair map cannot be transplanted onto human hair.

scenes.tts: So the idea carries over. Each class is most sensitive to its own part of a touch. The nervous system reads the pattern.
scenes.visual: The five icons return, press, motion, vibration, bent hair, slow stroke, and all classes light together beneath one touch.
scenes.narration: So the idea carries over. Each class is most sensitive to its own part of a touch. The nervous system reads the pattern.
